stem: What does nutrient antagonism mean in plant nutrition?
choices: A high level or imbalance of one ion can interfere with the uptake or use of another nutrient
It means increasing total EC causes nutrient ions to become proportionally less available to roots regardless of the identities and ratios of those ions
It describes the temporary decline in nutrient uptake that occurs when transpiration slows during the dark period, regardless of the nutrient mixture
It means micronutrients chemically neutralize macronutrients in the solution before those ions can reach the root surface and enter plant tissue
rationale: Nutrients interact. Excess or imbalance of one ion can reduce uptake or physiological use of another, which is why diagnosis should consider ratios and root-zone conditions rather than simply adding more fertilizer.
